adversary_breaks.expected: Exactly one terminal event per ticket; the loser returns offline.ticket_consumed / offline.ticket_released. Root cause (INFERRED from the migration): both RPCs and guard_offline_ledger_event() serialise only on pg_advisory_xact_lock(access_lock_key(v_uid)) — a per-CALLER lock — while identity recovery makes one ticket owned by two uids; the unique key is (ticket_id, event), so 'consumed' and 'released' rows never collide and the trigger's 'already has a terminal event' check is read-committed. The same shape (two callers, different locks) is what enforce_scored_shot_permit/consume rely on for conservation, so the ticket lock must be per ticket (or the ledger needs a one-terminal-per-ticket unique index).
adversary_breaks.observed: Account A (identity I) and account B (identity J) are both recreated after the original account (I+J) that allocated ticket T is deleted; both re-register the installation key and both recover T through issue_offline_grant(). consume_offline_ticket(T) on B overlapping release_offline_ticket(T) on A: consume=accepted, release=accepted, ledger for T = allocated,consumed,released (a scored shot exists AND a released row exists for the same ticket).
